source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ־בִּן־נ֠וּן מִֽן־הַשִּׁטִּ֞ים שְׁנַֽיִם־אֲנָשִׁ֤ים מְרַגְּלִים֙ חֶ֣רֶשׁ לֵאמֹ֔ר לְכ֛וּ רְא֥וּ אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ וְאֶת־יְרִיח֑וֹ וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ בֵּית־אִשָּׁ֥ה זוֹנָ֛ה וּשְׁמָ֥הּ רָחָ֖ב וַיִּשְׁכְּבוּ־שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Joshua son of Nun from the Shittim two men spying secretly, saying, go, see the land and Jericho. And they went and came [to the] house of a woman, a prostitute, and her name [was] Rahab, and they lay down there.

en.L: And Joshua son of Nun sent two men from Shittim as spies, secretly, saying, "Go, look over the land, and Jericho." And they went and came into the house of a woman, a prostitute, and her name [was] Rahab, and they lay down there.
en.B: Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men from Shittim to spy. "Go and look over the land," he told them, "and Jericho above all." So they set off and came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and they stayed the night there.
en.R: Joshua son of Nun was camped at Shittim. From there he sent out two men in secret to spy. He told them, "Go and look over the land, especially the city of Jericho." So the two men went. They came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab and stayed there for the night.

sw.L: Yoshua mwana wa Nuni akatuma kutoka Shitimu watu wawili kuwa wapelelezi kwa siri, akisema, "Nendeni, mkaitazame nchi, na Yeriko." Nao wakaenda, wakaingia katika nyumba ya mwanamke kahaba, na jina lake [lilikuwa] Rahabu, nao wakalala huko.
sw.B: Kisha Yoshua mwana wa Nuni aliwatuma watu wawili kwa siri kutoka Shitimu wakapeleleze. Aliwaambia, "Nendeni mkaitazame nchi, na hasa Yeriko." Basi wakaondoka, wakafika kwenye nyumba ya kahaba mmoja aitwaye Rahabu, wakalala huko usiku ule.
sw.R: Yoshua mwana wa Nuni alikuwa amepiga kambi huko Shitimu. Kutoka huko aliwatuma watu wawili kwa siri wakapeleleze. Aliwaambia, "Nendeni mkaitazame nchi, hasa mji wa Yeriko." Basi watu hao wawili walikwenda. Wakafika kwenye nyumba ya kahaba mmoja aitwaye Rahabu, wakalala huko usiku ule.

es.L: Y Josué hijo de Nun envió desde Sitim a dos hombres como espías, en secreto, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}}, {{plural_you:examinen|examinad}} la tierra, y Jericó». Y fueron y entraron en la casa de una mujer, una prostituta, cuyo nombre [era] Rahab, y se acostaron allí.
es.B: Entonces Josué hijo de Nun envió en secreto desde Sitim a dos hombres para espiar. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a examinar la tierra, y sobre todo Jericó». Ellos partieron y llegaron a la casa de una prostituta llamada Rahab, y pasaron allí la noche.
es.R: Josué hijo de Nun estaba acampado en Sitim. Desde allí envió en secreto a dos hombres para espiar. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a examinar la tierra, sobre todo la ciudad de Jericó». Así que los dos hombres fueron. Llegaron a la casa de una prostituta llamada Rahab y pasaron allí la noche.

decisions.choice: Shittim: Israel's last camp east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Shittim ("acacia trees") is on the plains of Moab, where Israel camped before crossing (Numbers 25:1; 33:49). The camp moves from there to the Jordan in 3:1.

decisions.choice: the land, and Jericho: Jericho in particular
alternatives: the land and the city of Jericho as two separate tasks
decisions.reason: The "and" picks out the first city in their path from the land as a whole. Jericho guarded the way up from the Jordan into the hill country.

decisions.choice: a woman who was a prostitute, named Rahab
decisions.reason: The word (zonah) is the ordinary word for a woman who sells sex (Genesis 38:15; Leviticus 21:7). An old Aramaic translation of Joshua calls her an innkeeper, perhaps to soften the story, but the Hebrew word does not mean that. The New Testament keeps the plain sense: it names "Rahab the prostitute" as an example of faith that acted (Hebrews 11:31; James 2:25). A stranger's coming and going at such a house would draw less notice.

decisions.choice: they lay down there: they lodged for the night
decisions.reason: The verb means to lie down, and in a setting like this it is the ordinary word for staying the night (verse 8 says they had not yet lain down to sleep). Nothing in the story says the men used her as a prostitute.

decisions.choice: a prostitute named Rahab
alternatives: a woman, a prostitute, whose name was Rahab
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a woman, a prostitute, and her name was Rahab"; Balanced and Readable join the three parts into one phrase, and Literal keeps them.

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Nun was camped at Shittim
decisions.reason: Readable says what Shittim was, so the reader knows where the spies started (m1).

decisions.choice: "Rahabu", "kahaba", "Yeriko", "Shitimu"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua: "Rahabu yule kahaba" and "Yeriko" are the forms already published in the Swahili of Hebrews 11:30-31 and James 2:25, so the book keeps them. "Kahaba" is the plain, standard word for a prostitute; "malaya" is coarser.

decisions.choice: "Rahab", "prostituta"
decisions.reason: The name keeps the form Spanish already uses in Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25, where she is "Rahab la prostituta". "Prostituta" is the plain word for the Hebrew zonah, as in those passages.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣אָמַ֔ר לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיח֖וֹ לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה אֲ֠נָשִׁים בָּ֣אוּ הֵ֧נָּה הַלַּ֛יְלָה מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לַחְפֹּ֥ר אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was said to [the] king of Jericho, saying, look, men have come here tonight from [the] sons of Israel to search out the land.

en.L: And it was told to the king of Jericho, saying, "Look, men have come here tonight from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel to search out the land."
en.B: The king of Jericho was told, "Some men from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} have come here tonight to search out the land."
en.R: Someone told the king of Jericho, "Listen! Some men from Israel came here tonight. They have come to find out about our land."

sw.L: Mfalme wa Yeriko akaambiwa, akisema, "Tazama, watu wamekuja hapa usiku huu kutoka kwa wana wa Israeli ili kuipeleleza nchi."
sw.B: Mfalme wa Yeriko aliambiwa, "Watu fulani wa Waisraeli wamekuja hapa usiku huu kuipeleleza nchi."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja alimwambia mfalme wa Yeriko, "Sikiliza! Watu kutoka Israeli wamekuja hapa usiku huu. Wamekuja kuipeleleza nchi yetu."

es.L: Y se le dijo al rey de Jericó: «Mira, unos hombres de los hijos de Israel han venido aquí esta noche para explorar la tierra».
es.B: Al rey de Jericó le avisaron: «Unos hombres de los israelitas han venido aquí esta noche para explorar la tierra».
es.R: Alguien le dijo al rey de Jericó: «¡Escucha! Unos hombres de Israel llegaron aquí esta noche. Han venido para averiguar cómo es nuestra tierra».

decisions.choice: the king of Jericho: the ruler of a city-state
decisions.reason: Canaan was divided among many small cities, each with its own king (12:9-24 lists thirty-one of them). Jericho's king ruled the city and the land around it.

decisions.choice: to search out the land: to explore it for an attack
decisions.reason: The verb (chafar) means to dig or search; here it is to find out the land's ways in, as in Deuteronomy 1:22.

decisions.choice: men from Israel
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the sentence short; the people are the same.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרִיח֔וֹ אֶל־רָחָ֖ב לֵאמֹ֑ר ה֠וֹצִיאִי הָאֲנָשִׁ֨ים הַבָּאִ֤ים אֵלַ֨יִךְ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣אוּ לְבֵיתֵ֔ךְ כִּ֛י לַחְפֹּ֥ר אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent [the] king of Jericho to Rahab, saying, bring out the men, the [ones] coming to you who came into your house, for to search out all the land they have come.

en.L: And the king of Jericho sent to Rahab, saying, "Bring out the men who came to you, who came into your house, for they have come to search out all the land."
en.B: So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the visitors who came to you and went into your house. They have come to spy out the whole land."
en.R: So the king sent a message to Rahab. It said, "Bring out the men who came to your house. They are spies. They have come to look over our whole land."

sw.L: Mfalme wa Yeriko akatuma kwa Rahabu, akisema, "Watoe watu waliokuja kwako, walioingia nyumbani mwako, kwa maana wamekuja kuipeleleza nchi yote."
sw.B: Basi mfalme wa Yeriko alituma ujumbe kwa Rahabu: "Watoe wageni waliokuja kwako na kuingia nyumbani mwako. Wamekuja kuipeleleza nchi yote."
sw.R: Basi mfalme alituma ujumbe kwa Rahabu. Ulisema, "Watoe watu waliokuja nyumbani kwako. Ni wapelelezi. Wamekuja kuipeleleza nchi yetu yote."

es.L: Y el rey de Jericó envió a Rahab, diciendo: «Saca a los hombres que vinieron a ti, que entraron en tu casa, porque han venido a explorar toda la tierra».
es.B: Entonces el rey de Jericó le mandó este mensaje a Rahab: «Saca a los visitantes que llegaron a ti y entraron en tu casa. Han venido a espiar toda la tierra».
es.R: Entonces el rey le envió un mensaje a Rahab. Decía: «Saca a los hombres que llegaron a tu casa. Son espías. Han venido a examinar toda nuestra tierra».

decisions.choice: who came to you, who came into your house: said twice for force
decisions.reason: The king's message names the men twice over, as if to leave Rahab no room to deny they were there.

decisions.choice: They are spies.
decisions.reason: Readable states plainly what "to search out the land" means here.

source.text: וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָֽאִשָּׁ֛ה אֶת־שְׁנֵ֥י הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַֽתִּצְפְּנ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר׀כֵּ֗ן בָּ֤אוּ אֵלַי֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְתִּי מֵאַ֥יִן הֵֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And took the woman the two men and hid him, and she said, so, came to me the men, and not I knew from where they [were].

en.L: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. And she said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they [were] from.
en.B: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. "It is true, the men did come to me," she said, "but I did not know where they came from.
en.R: But Rahab had already hidden the two men. She answered, "Yes, the men came to my house. But I did not know where they were from.

sw.L: Lakini yule mwanamke alikuwa amewachukua wale watu wawili na kuwaficha. Naye akasema, "Ndiyo, watu hao walikuja kwangu, lakini sikujua walikotoka.
sw.B: Lakini mwanamke huyo alikuwa amewachukua wale watu wawili na kuwaficha. Akasema, "Ni kweli, watu hao walikuja kwangu, lakini sikujua walikotoka.
sw.R: Lakini Rahabu alikuwa amekwisha kuwaficha wale watu wawili. Akajibu, "Ndiyo, watu hao walikuja nyumbani kwangu. Lakini sikujua walikotoka.

es.L: Pero la mujer había tomado a los dos hombres y los había escondido. Y dijo: «Sí, los hombres vinieron a mí, pero no sabía de dónde [eran].
es.B: Pero la mujer ya había tomado a los dos hombres y los había escondido. Ella dijo: «Es cierto que los hombres vinieron a mí, pero yo no sabía de dónde venían.
es.R: Pero Rahab ya había escondido a los dos hombres. Ella respondió: «Sí, los hombres vinieron a mi casa. Pero yo no sabía de dónde eran.

decisions.choice: had taken ... and hidden them: done before the king's men arrived
alternatives: took and hid them then, while the messengers waited
decisions.reason: The verbs simply carry the story on, but she cannot hide the men in front of the king's messengers. The narrator goes back to tell what she had already done; verse 6 says how.

decisions.choice: hid them: literally "hid him"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pronoun is singular. It may mean she hid each man in turn, or it may treat the pair as one group; the sense is that both were hidden.

decisions.choice: Rahab's answer: a deliberate deception
decisions.reason: Rahab admits what cannot be denied and lies about the rest (verse 5). The story tells it without comment; later Scripture praises her faith and her receiving the spies (Hebrews 11:31; James 2:25), not the lie as such.

decisions.choice: It is true
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word (ken, "so, right") grants the point. Balanced lets her concede it before she misleads them.

source.text: וַיְהִ֨י הַשַּׁ֜עַר לִסְגּ֗וֹר בַּחֹ֨שֶׁךְ֙ וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים יָצָ֔אוּ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי אָ֥נָה הָלְכ֖וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֑ים רִדְפ֥וּ מַהֵ֛ר אַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם כִּ֥י תַשִּׂיגֽוּם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was [that] the gate [was] to shut at the darkness, and the men went out; not I know where went the men. Pursue quickly after them, for you will overtake them.

en.L: And it was [time] for the gate to be shut at dark, and the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Pursue them quickly, for you will overtake them."
en.B: When the gate was about to be shut at dark, the men left. I do not know where they went. Go after them quickly. You will catch them."
en.R: When it got dark and it was time to close the city gate, the men left. I do not know where they went. Hurry and chase them! You can still catch them."

sw.L: Ikawa [wakati] lango lilipokaribia kufungwa gizani, watu hao wakatoka. Sijui watu hao walikokwenda. Wafuatieni upesi, kwa maana mtawapata."
sw.B: Lango lilipokaribia kufungwa giza lilipoingia, watu hao waliondoka. Sijui walikokwenda. Wafuateni upesi, mtawakuta."
sw.R: Giza lilipoingia na ukawa wakati wa kufunga lango la mji, watu hao waliondoka. Sijui walikokwenda. Fanyeni haraka, mwakimbize! Bado mnaweza kuwakamata."

es.L: Y era [hora] de cerrar la puerta al oscurecer, y los hombres salieron. No sé adónde fueron los hombres. {{plural_you:Persíganlos|Perseguidlos}} pronto, porque los {{plural_you:alcanzarán|alcanzaréis}}».
es.B: Cuando iban a cerrar la puerta, al oscurecer, los hombres se fueron. No sé adónde fueron. {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} tras ellos enseguida. Los {{plural_you:alcanzarán|alcanzaréis}}».
es.R: Cuando oscureció y era hora de cerrar la puerta de la ciudad, los hombres se fueron. No sé adónde fueron. ¡{{plural_you:Dense prisa|Daos prisa}} y {{plural_you:persíganlos|perseguidlos}}! Todavía {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} alcanzarlos».

decisions.choice: the gate was to be shut at dark
decisions.reason: A walled city closed its gate at nightfall for safety (Nehemiah 7:3). Rahab claims the men left just before it closed, so they must already be outside the city.

decisions.choice: for you will overtake them: a reason to hurry
decisions.reason: She urges speed by promising success: they are not far ahead.

source.text: וְהִ֖יא הֶעֱלָ֣תַם הַגָּ֑גָה וַֽתִּטְמְנֵם֙ בְּפִשְׁתֵּ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ הָעֲרֻכ֥וֹת לָ֖הּ עַל־הַגָּֽג׃

records.literal_gloss: And she, she had brought them up to the roof and hid them in [the] flax of the wood, the [ones] laid out by her on the roof.

en.L: But she had brought them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.
en.B: In fact she had brought them up to the roof and covered them with the flax stalks she had spread out there.
en.R: Rahab had really taken the men up to her flat roof. She had hidden them under stalks of flax that she had spread out there to dry.

sw.L: Lakini yeye alikuwa amewapandisha juu ya dari na kuwaficha katikati ya mabua ya kitani, aliyokuwa ameyapanga juu ya dari.
sw.B: Kwa kweli alikuwa amewapandisha juu ya dari ya nyumba na kuwafunika kwa mabua ya kitani aliyokuwa ameyatandaza huko.
sw.R: Kumbe Rahabu alikuwa amewapeleka wale watu juu ya dari tambarare ya nyumba yake. Alikuwa amewaficha chini ya mabua ya kitani aliyoyatandaza huko yakauke.

es.L: Pero ella los había hecho subir a la azotea y los había escondido entre los tallos de lino que tenía extendidos sobre la azotea.
es.B: En realidad, ella los había subido a la azotea y los había tapado con los tallos de lino que había extendido allí.
es.R: En realidad, Rahab había llevado a los hombres a la azotea plana de su casa. Los había escondido debajo de unos tallos de lino que había puesto allí para que se secaran.

decisions.choice: she had brought them up: told now, done earlier
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with "she" and breaks the run of the story, the Hebrew way of giving background. It explains the hiding of verse 4.

decisions.choice: stalks of flax laid out on the roof
decisions.reason: Roofs were flat and were used for work and sleep (1 Samuel 9:25-26). Flax was pulled in spring (Exodus 9:31) and laid out to dry before its fibers were made into linen. The season fits the crossing at the time of harvest (3:15) and Passover (5:10).

decisions.choice: flat roof ... to dry
decisions.reason: Readable adds what a reader needs to picture the scene (m2).

source.text: וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים רָדְפ֤וּ אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן עַ֖ל הַֽמַּעְבְּר֑וֹת וְהַשַּׁ֣עַר סָגָ֔רוּ אַחֲרֵ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָצְא֥וּ הָרֹדְפִ֖ים אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the men pursued after them [the] way of the Jordan to the fords, and the gate they shut after as the pursuers had gone out after them.

en.L: And the men pursued them on the road to the Jordan, as far as the fords; and they shut the gate after the pursuers had gone out after them.
en.B: So the men set out after them along the road to the Jordan, as far as the river crossings, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.
en.R: So the king's men went after the spies. They took the road toward the Jordan River and went as far as the places where people cross it. As soon as they had gone out, the city gate was shut.

sw.L: Nao watu hao wakawafuatia katika njia iendayo Yordani, hadi vivukoni; na lango likafungwa baada ya hao waliowafuatia kutoka nje kuwafuata.
sw.B: Basi watu hao waliwafuatia katika njia iendayo Yordani, hadi kwenye vivuko vya mto. Mara tu wale waliowafuatia walipotoka, lango likafungwa.
sw.R: Basi watu wa mfalme waliwafuata wale wapelelezi. Walishika njia iendayo Mto Yordani, wakafika hadi mahali ambapo watu huvuka mto. Mara tu walipotoka nje, lango la mji likafungwa.

es.L: Y los hombres los persiguieron por el camino del Jordán, hasta los vados; y cerraron la puerta después de que salieron tras ellos los perseguidores.
es.B: Entonces los hombres salieron tras ellos por el camino que lleva al Jordán, hasta los pasos del río, y en cuanto salieron los perseguidores, se cerró la puerta.
es.R: Así que los hombres del rey fueron tras los espías. Tomaron el camino hacia el río Jordán y llegaron hasta los lugares por donde la gente lo cruza. En cuanto ellos salieron, se cerró la puerta de la ciudad.

decisions.choice: the fords: shallow places where the Jordan could be crossed
decisions.reason: The pursuers assume the spies are heading back east to Israel's camp. The river was in flood at this season (3:15), so the fords were the only way over.

decisions.choice: the gate shut behind the pursuers
decisions.reason: The closed gate shuts the spies inside the city; their only way out is the one Rahab gives them (verse 15).

decisions.choice: river crossings (B); places where people cross it (R)
decisions.reason: "Fords" is less familiar to many readers; the meaning is the same.

source.text: וְהֵ֖מָּה טֶ֣רֶם יִשְׁכָּב֑וּן וְהִ֛יא עָלְתָ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־הַגָּֽג׃

records.literal_gloss: And they, before they lay down, and she went up to them on the roof,

en.L: And before they lay down, she came up to them on the roof,
en.B: Before the men lay down to sleep, she came up to them on the roof
en.R: Before the spies lay down to sleep, Rahab went up to them on the roof.

sw.L: Nao kabla hawajalala, yeye alipanda kwao juu ya dari,
sw.B: Kabla watu hao hawajalala, Rahabu alipanda kwao juu ya dari,
sw.R: Kabla wale wapelelezi hawajalala, Rahabu alipanda kwao juu ya dari.

es.L: Y antes de que ellos se acostaran, ella subió a donde estaban, a la azotea,
es.B: Antes de que los hombres se acostaran a dormir, ella subió a la azotea, donde estaban,
es.R: Antes de que los espías se acostaran a dormir, Rahab subió a la azotea, donde estaban ellos.

decisions.choice: before they lay down: before they settled for the night
decisions.reason: This takes up "they lay down there" from verse 1: the men had not yet gone to sleep when she came to them.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי־נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכִֽי־נָפְלָ֤ה אֵֽימַתְכֶם֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְכִ֥י נָמֹ֛גוּ כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ מִפְּנֵיכֶֽם׃

decisions.choice: I know that the LORD has given you the land
decisions.reason: Rahab, a Canaanite, speaks of Israel's God by his name and says first what his promise has already settled (1:2-3). The spies repeat her words to Joshua (verse 24).

decisions.choice: dread has fallen ... melt away: the words of the Song of the Sea
decisions.reason: Moses' song foretold that the people of Canaan would melt away and that dread and fear would fall on them (Exodus 15:15-16; see Deuteronomy 2:25; 11:25). Rahab says it has happened.

decisions.choice: melt away: lose all courage
decisions.reason: A heart that melts is one that has lost its courage (verse 11; 5:1; Deuteronomy 20:8).

decisions.choice: melting in fear (B); weak with fear (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture and adds "in fear" so it is clear; Readable gives its sense (m3).

decisions.choice: plural "you" (ustedes / vosotros) when Rahab speaks to the spies
decisions.reason: Rahab speaks to the two men together, so Spanish uses the plural forms; the spies answer her with "tú", and the king's message to her also uses "tú".

source.text: כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ אֵ֠ת אֲשֶׁר־הוֹבִ֨ישׁ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־מֵ֤י יַם־סוּף֙ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֔ם בְּצֵאתְכֶ֖ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֡ם לִשְׁנֵי֩ מַלְכֵ֨י הָאֱמֹרִ֜י אֲשֶׁ֨ר בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ לְסִיחֹ֣ן וּלְע֔וֹג אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱרַמְתֶּ֖ם אוֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For we have heard how dried up YHWH [the] waters of [the] Sea of Reeds before you when you came out from Egypt, and what you did to [the] two kings of the Amorite[s] who [were] across the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you devoted to destruction.

en.L: For we have heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
en.B: We have heard how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the water of the Red Sea dry up before you as you left Egypt. And we have heard how you dealt with the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, Sihon and Og: you devoted them to destruction.
en.R: We heard that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the Red Sea dry up for you when you came out of Egypt. We also heard what you did to Sihon and Og, the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River. You destroyed them completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana tumesikia jinsi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoyakausha maji ya Bahari ya Matete mbele yenu mlipotoka Misri, na mambo mliyowatendea wafalme wawili wa Waamori waliokuwa ng'ambo ya Yordani, Sihoni na Ogu, ambao mliwaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi.
sw.B: Tumesikia jinsi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyoyakausha maji ya Bahari ya Shamu mbele yenu mlipotoka Misri. Tena tumesikia mlivyowatendea wale wafalme wawili wa Waamori ng'ambo ya Yordani, Sihoni na Ogu: mliwaweka wakfu kwa maangamizi.
sw.R: Tulisikia kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliikausha Bahari ya Shamu kwa ajili yenu mlipotoka Misri. Tulisikia pia mambo mliyowatendea Sihoni na Ogu, wafalme wawili wa Waamori upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani. Mliwaangamiza kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

es.L: Porque hemos oído cómo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} secó las aguas del mar de los Juncos delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando {{plural_you:salieron|salisteis}} de Egipto, y lo que {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} a los dos reyes de los amorreos que [estaban] al otro lado del Jordán, a Sijón y a Og, a quienes {{plural_you:consagraron|consagrasteis}} al exterminio.
es.B: Hemos oído cómo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} secó el agua del mar Rojo delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando {{plural_you:salieron|salisteis}} de Egipto. Y hemos oído lo que {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} con los dos reyes amorreos del otro lado del Jordán, Sijón y Og: los {{plural_you:consagraron|consagrasteis}} al exterminio.
es.R: Oímos que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} secó el mar Rojo para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando {{plural_you:salieron|salisteis}} de Egipto. También oímos lo que les {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} a Sijón y a Og, los dos reyes amorreos del otro lado del río Jordán, al este. {{plural_you:Los destruyeron|Los destruisteis}} por completo, como pueblos entregados {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: the LORD dried up the Sea of Reeds
decisions.reason: The crossing of the sea (Exodus 14:21-22) happened forty years earlier, and the news still frightens Canaan. In 4:23 Joshua sets the crossing of the Jordan beside it.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: here, east of it
decisions.reason: The phrase names the far side of the river from where the speaker stands. Rahab is in Jericho, west of the Jordan, so she means the land east of it, where Sihon and Og ruled.

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites
decisions.reason: Israel defeated Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan and took their lands (Numbers 21:21-35; Deuteronomy 2:26-3:11).

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction: given over to God completely
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for a "devoted thing" (Leviticus 27:28-29). In war it means a people was destroyed and none were kept for gain, as with Sihon and Og (Deuteronomy 2:34; 3:6).

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name is "Sea of Reeds", which Literal keeps. Balanced and Readable use the familiar name for the sea Israel crossed, as Exodus does.

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable explains the term as in Deuteronomy 2:34 (m4).

decisions.choice: "kuweka wakfu kwa maangamizi" (L, B); "kuangamiza kabisa, kama watu waliotolewa kwa BWANA" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua, as in Deuteronomy: herem is giving people or things over wholly to God, so that nothing is kept for oneself. Literal and Balanced say "kuweka wakfu kwa maangamizi" (to set apart for destruction), and the devoted thing is "kitu kilichowekwa wakfu kwa maangamizi"; Readable says "kuangamiza kabisa" and names the LORD, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Bahari ya Matete" (L); "Bahari ya Shamu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds"; Balanced and Readable use "Bahari ya Shamu", the name Swahili readers know, as the English says "the Red Sea".

decisions.choice: "consagrar al exterminio" (Literal, Balanced); "destruir por completo, como pueblos entregados al SEÑOR" (Readable)
decisions.reason: This is the first use in Joshua of the Hebrew herem, to give something over to God by destroying it. Following the terms note for these books, Literal and Balanced say "consagrar al exterminio" and the thing so given is "lo consagrado al exterminio"; Readable says "destruir por completo" and, as the English does, explains whom it was given over to.

source.text: וַנִּשְׁמַע֙ וַיִּמַּ֣ס לְבָבֵ֔נוּ וְלֹא־קָ֨מָה ע֥וֹד ר֛וּחַ בְּאִ֖ישׁ מִפְּנֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם ה֤וּא אֱלֹהִים֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם מִמַּ֔עַל וְעַל־הָאָ֖רֶץ מִתָּֽחַת׃

records.literal_gloss: And we heard, and melted our heart, and not rose again spirit in [any] man because of you, for YHWH your God, he [is] God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.

en.L: And we heard, and our heart melted, and there did not rise up any more spirit in anyone because of you; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] God in the heavens above and on the earth beneath.
en.B: When we heard it, our hearts melted, and no one had any courage left because of you, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.
en.R: When we heard these things, we were filled with fear. No one has any courage left to fight you, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is God of the heavens above and of the earth below.

sw.L: Tukasikia, na moyo wetu ukayeyuka, wala haikuinuka tena roho ndani ya mtu yeyote kwa sababu yenu; kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} [ni] Mungu katika mbingu juu na katika nchi chini.
sw.B: Tuliposikia hayo mioyo yetu iliyeyuka, wala hakuna mtu aliyebaki na ujasiri kwa sababu yenu, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu ndiye Mungu mbinguni juu na duniani chini.
sw.R: Tuliposikia mambo hayo, tulijawa na hofu. Hakuna mtu aliyebaki na ujasiri wa kupigana nanyi, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu ndiye Mungu wa mbingu zilizo juu na wa dunia iliyo chini.

es.L: Y lo oímos, y se derritió nuestro corazón, y ya no se levantó ánimo en nadie por causa de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} [es] Dios arriba en los cielos y abajo en la tierra.
es.B: Al oírlo, se nos derritió el corazón, y a nadie le quedó valor por causa de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} es Dios arriba en el cielo y abajo en la tierra.
es.R: Cuando oímos estas cosas, nos llenamos de miedo. A nadie le queda valor para pelear contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} es Dios de los cielos, arriba, y de la tierra, abajo.

decisions.choice: no spirit rose up in anyone: no one had courage left
decisions.reason: "Spirit" (ruach) here is a person's breath and vigor; when it does not rise, a person has no will to stand and fight (5:1; 1 Kings 10:5).

decisions.choice: the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on earth beneath
decisions.reason: Rahab's confession uses the words Moses gave Israel to confess (Deuteronomy 4:39). She owns the LORD not as one god among the gods of the nations but as God of all places.

decisions.choice: our hearts melted (B); we were filled with fear (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew picture; Readable gives its sense, since the next clause speaks of courage (m1).

decisions.choice: your God is God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the subject ("he") for emphasis; Literal keeps it, and Balanced and Readable carry the stress in the sentence itself.

decisions.choice: to fight you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the courage would have been for.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּֽׁבְעוּ־נָ֥א לִי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה כִּי־עָשִׂ֥יתִי עִמָּכֶ֖ם חָ֑סֶד וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם גַּם־אַתֶּ֜ם עִם־בֵּ֤ית אָבִי֙ חֶ֔סֶד וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם לִ֖י א֥וֹת אֱמֶֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, swear, please, to me by YHWH, since I have done with you steadfast love, that will do also you with [the] house of my father steadfast love, and give to me a sign of truth,

en.L: And now, please swear to me by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, since I have shown you steadfast love, that you also will show steadfast love to my father's house, and give me a sure sign,
en.B: So now, swear to me by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: since I have shown you faithful love, you too will show faithful love to my father's family. Give me a sign I can trust
en.R: I have shown you faithful love. So now, make a promise to me in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Promise that you will show faithful love to my family too. Give me a sign that I can trust.

sw.L: Basi sasa, tafadhali niapieni kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa kuwa nimewatendea fadhili, kwamba ninyi pia mtaitendea fadhili nyumba ya baba yangu, na kunipa ishara ya kweli,
sw.B: Basi sasa, niapieni kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: kwa kuwa nimewatendea fadhili, ninyi pia mtaitendea fadhili jamaa ya baba yangu. Nipeni ishara ninayoweza kuitegemea
sw.R: Nimewatendea fadhili. Basi sasa, niahidini kwa jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Ahidini kwamba ninyi pia mtaitendea fadhili jamaa yangu. Nipeni ishara ninayoweza kuiamini.

es.L: Y ahora, por favor, {{plural_you:júrenme|juradme}} por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que, ya que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he mostrado amor leal, también {{plural_you:ustedes mostrarán|vosotros mostraréis}} amor leal a la casa de mi padre, y {{plural_you:denme|dadme}} una señal segura,
es.B: Así que ahora, {{plural_you:júrenme|juradme}} por {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} que, ya que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he mostrado amor fiel, también {{plural_you:ustedes mostrarán|vosotros mostraréis}} amor fiel a la familia de mi padre. {{plural_you:Denme|Dadme}} una señal segura
es.R: Yo {{plural_you:les|os}} he mostrado amor fiel. Así que ahora {{plural_you:prométanme|prometedme}} en el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que también {{plural_you:mostrarán|mostraréis}} amor fiel a mi familia. {{plural_you:Denme|Dadme}} una señal en la que yo pueda confiar.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal kindness that keeps faith
decisions.reason: Chesed is goodness shown out of loyalty, the faithfulness one party owes another in a bond. Rahab has acted as the spies' loyal friend, and she asks that the same be done for her family. The word is used of the LORD's covenant love (Exodus 34:6; Deuteronomy 7:9).

decisions.choice: swear to me by the LORD: an oath that calls God to witness
decisions.reason: To swear by the LORD bound the spies before their own God, the one Rahab has just confessed (verse 11). Israel was to swear by his name alone (Deuteronomy 6:13).

decisions.choice: a sign of truth: a sure pledge
alternatives: a token that can be relied on
decisions.reason: "Truth" (emet) here is reliability: something she can hold them to. The oath itself (verse 14) and the scarlet cord (verse 18) give her that assurance.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6 and Deuteronomy, so that the loyalty in the word is kept; "kindness" alone would leave it out.

decisions.choice: my father's family (B); my family (R)
decisions.reason: "House" means the household, the family under its head; verse 13 lists who is meant.

decisions.choice: "fadhili" at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Joshua, following the terms note for these books: hesed shown between people is "fadhili", loyal kindness that keeps faith; "upendo usiokoma" is kept for God's steadfast love. The English says "steadfast love" (Literal) and "faithful love" (Balanced, Readable); Swahili uses the one word at every level.

decisions.choice: "amor leal" (Literal); "amor fiel" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew hesed is the loyal kindness that keeps faith. Spanish follows the words already settled for it in Psalms and in the terms note for these books, and uses them where the English has "steadfast love" and "faithful love", here and in verse 14.

en.B: that you will keep my father and mother alive, with my brothers and sisters and all their people, and rescue us from death."
en.R: Promise that you will let my father and mother live, and my brothers and sisters, and all their families. Save us from being killed."

es.L: y que {{plural_you:dejarán|dejaréis}} con vida a mi padre y a mi madre y a mis hermanos y a mis hermanas y a todos los suyos, y {{plural_you:librarán|libraréis}} nuestras vidas de la muerte».
es.B: de que {{plural_you:dejarán|dejaréis}} con vida a mi padre y a mi madre, junto con mis hermanos y hermanas y toda su gente, y nos {{plural_you:librarán|libraréis}} de la muerte».

decisions.choice: all who belong to them: their households
decisions.reason: The phrase can take in goods as well as people, but the point is life and death, so their wives, children and dependants are meant (6:23).

decisions.choice: our lives: literally "our souls"
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) means the living person. To deliver someone's nefesh from death is to keep that person alive.

decisions.choice: all their families
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ לָ֣הּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים נַפְשֵׁ֤נוּ תַחְתֵּיכֶם֙ לָמ֔וּת אִ֚ם לֹ֣א תַגִּ֔ידוּ אֶת־דְּבָרֵ֖נוּ זֶ֑ה וְהָיָ֗ה בְּתֵת־יְהוָ֥ה לָ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעָשִׂ֥ינוּ עִמָּ֖ךְ חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her the men, our life in place of you[rs] to die, if not you tell this business of ours; and it will be, when gives YHWH to us the land, and we will do with you steadfast love and truth.

en.L: And the men said to her, "Our life for yours, to death, if you do not tell this business of ours! And when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives us the land, we will deal with you in steadfast love and faithfulness."
en.B: The men answered her, "We stake our lives on yours, even to death, so long as you do not tell anyone about our mission. When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives us the land, we will treat you with faithful love and keep our word."
en.R: The men answered, "If anything happens to you, may we die in your place! But you must not tell anyone what we are doing. When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives us this land, we will show you faithful love and keep our promise."

sw.L: Wale watu wakamwambia, "Uhai wetu badala ya wenu hadi kufa, ikiwa hamtalitangaza jambo hili letu! Na itakuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakapotupa nchi, tutakutendea fadhili na uaminifu."

es.L: Y los hombres le dijeron: «¡Nuestra vida por la tuya, hasta la muerte, si no cuentas este asunto nuestro! Y cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos dé la tierra, te trataremos con amor leal y fidelidad».
es.B: Los hombres le respondieron: «Respondemos con nuestra vida por la tuya, hasta la muerte, con tal de que no cuentes a nadie nuestra misión. Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos dé la tierra, te trataremos con amor fiel y cumpliremos nuestra palabra».
es.R: Los hombres le respondieron: «¡Si algo te pasa, que muramos nosotros en tu lugar! Pero no debes contarle a nadie lo que estamos haciendo. Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos dé esta tierra, te mostraremos amor fiel y cumpliremos nuestra promesa».

decisions.choice: our life for yours, to death: the spies pledge their own lives
alternatives: our lives will be forfeit if you die
decisions.reason: It is a form of oath: if harm comes to Rahab's family through Israel, the spies' own lives are owed in exchange (compare 1 Kings 20:39, 42).

decisions.choice: this business of ours: the spies' mission
decisions.reason: The word (davar) is "word" or "matter". She must not report their errand to the king, or the oath no longer binds them (verse 20).

decisions.choice: steadfast love and faithfulness: loyalty that will be carried out
decisions.reason: The pair (chesed and emet) is used of the LORD's own covenant faithfulness (Exodus 34:6) and of a promise that will truly be kept (Genesis 24:49; 47:29). The spies answer Rahab's request (verse 12) with her own word and promise that it will be kept.

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 34:6 and Deuteronomy, so that the loyalty in the word is kept; "kindness" alone would leave it out.

decisions.choice: keep our word (B); keep our promise (R)
decisions.reason: Emet here is the reliability of the oath; Balanced and Readable say it as a promise kept (m3).

sw.L: Ndipo akawateremsha kwa kamba kupitia dirishani, kwa maana nyumba yake [ilikuwa] ubavuni mwa ukuta wa mji, naye aliishi ukutani.

es.L: Entonces ella los bajó con una cuerda por la ventana, porque su casa [estaba] en el costado de la muralla, y ella vivía en la muralla.
es.B: Entonces ella los descolgó con una cuerda por la ventana, porque su casa estaba construida en la muralla de la ciudad; vivía en la muralla misma.
es.R: La casa de Rahab estaba construida en la muralla de la ciudad. Por eso ella usó una cuerda para bajar a los hombres por su ventana hacia afuera.

decisions.choice: her house was in the wall
decisions.reason: Houses could be built into or against a city's wall, so a window in the back wall opened outside the city. With the gate shut (verse 7), that window was the spies' way out. David escaped from his house the same way (1 Samuel 19:12).

decisions.choice: she let them down: the event told ahead of the talk that follows
alternatives: she spoke to them from the window after letting them down
decisions.reason: Verses 16-21 report what was said, and they speak of "the window through which you let us down" (verse 18). The narrator may tell the escape first and then go back to the words spoken before it, or the conversation may have been called down from the window.

decisions.choice: the reason first, then the escape
decisions.reason: Readable puts the house in the wall first so that the escape makes sense as it is read.

decisions.reason: The pursuers had gone east toward the Jordan (verse 7). The rough hills rising west of Jericho, the other way, had many places to hide.

decisions.choice: three days: long enough for the search to end
decisions.reason: By then the pursuers would give up and return (verse 22). The phrase may count parts of days, as in 1:11 and 3:2.

decisions.reason: The word (naqi) means clean, clear of guilt or duty. The spies set out conditions in verses 18-20; if Rahab does not keep them, the oath will not bind them.

decisions.choice: unless you do these things

decisions.choice: look, we are coming: when we come
decisions.reason: "Look" (hinneh) points to what is about to happen. The spies set the terms that will hold on the day of attack.

decisions.choice: a cord of scarlet thread: a sign that marks the house
decisions.reason: Scarlet thread was dyed bright red and was costly (Exodus 25:4; Genesis 38:28). Hanging from the window in the wall, it would show the attackers which house to spare.

decisions.choice: cord: a word that elsewhere also means "hope"
decisions.reason: The word for this cord (tiqvah) is the same as the common word for hope, and is found meaning "cord" only here and in verse 21. Whether a play on the two senses is meant is uncertain.

decisions.choice: gathered into the marked house: the pattern of Passover
decisions.reason: As at the first Passover, a family is saved by staying inside a house marked with red while judgment falls outside, and anyone who goes out of its door is not protected (verse 19; Exodus 12:7, 13, 22). The text does not draw the link itself.

decisions.choice: unless
decisions.reason: In Balanced the conditions finish the sentence begun in verse 17: the oath does not bind them unless she does these things.

decisions.choice: red rope
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for color and cord.

records.literal_gloss: And it will be [that] every [one] who goes out from [the] doors of your house to the outside, his blood [will be] on his head, and we [will be] free; and every [one] who will be with you in the house, his blood [will be] on our head, if a hand will be on him.

en.L: And it will be [that] anyone who goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood [will be] on his own head, and we [will be] free; but anyone who is with you in the house, his blood [will be] on our head, if a hand is laid on him.
en.B: Anyone who goes out through the doors of your house into the street will be responsible for their own death, and we will be free of blame. But if anyone who is with you in the house is harmed, the blame for their death will be on us.
en.R: If anyone goes out of your house into the street and is killed, it will be their own fault. We will not be to blame. But if anyone inside the house with you is hurt, we will be to blame.

sw.L: Na itakuwa kila atakayetoka nje ya milango ya nyumba yako akaenda njiani, damu yake [itakuwa] juu ya kichwa chake, nasi [tutakuwa] bila hatia; lakini kila atakayekuwa pamoja nawe ndani ya nyumba, damu yake [itakuwa] juu ya vichwa vyetu, ikiwa mkono utawekwa juu yake.
sw.B: Mtu yeyote atakayetoka nje ya milango ya nyumba yako akaenda barabarani atawajibika kwa kifo chake mwenyewe, nasi hatutakuwa na hatia. Lakini mtu yeyote aliye pamoja nawe ndani ya nyumba akidhurika, hatia ya kifo chake itakuwa juu yetu.
sw.R: Mtu yeyote akitoka nje ya nyumba yako akaenda barabarani na kuuawa, ni kosa lake mwenyewe. Sisi hatutakuwa na hatia. Lakini mtu yeyote aliye ndani ya nyumba pamoja nawe akiumizwa, hatia itakuwa yetu.

es.L: Y sucederá que cualquiera que salga de las puertas de tu casa a la calle, su sangre [será] sobre su propia cabeza, y nosotros [seremos] libres; pero cualquiera que esté contigo en la casa, su sangre [será] sobre nuestra cabeza, si se le pone mano encima.
es.B: Cualquiera que salga por las puertas de tu casa a la calle será responsable de su propia muerte, y nosotros quedaremos libres de culpa. Pero si alguien que esté contigo en la casa sufre daño, la culpa de su muerte caerá sobre nosotros.
es.R: Si alguien sale de tu casa a la calle y lo matan, será culpa suya. Nosotros no tendremos la culpa. Pero si alguien que esté contigo dentro de la casa sufre daño, la culpa será nuestra.

decisions.choice: his blood on his head: he bears the guilt for his own death
decisions.reason: Blood that is "on someone's head" is guilt for a death laid on that person (2 Samuel 1:16; 1 Kings 2:37). Whoever leaves the house has no claim on the oath; whoever stays in it is the spies' responsibility.

decisions.choice: if a hand is on him: if anyone harms him
decisions.reason: To lay a hand on someone is to attack or harm that person (Genesis 37:22, 27).

decisions.choice: free: clear of guilt
decisions.reason: The same word as "free" from the oath (verse 17): the spies will owe nothing for that death.

decisions.choice: responsible for their own death (B); their own fault (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m1); Literal keeps it. "Their" refers to "anyone", man or woman.

en.B: So they went into the hills and stayed there three days, until the men chasing them had gone back. The pursuers had searched all along the road without finding them.
en.R: The spies went into the hills and hid there for three days. The king's men searched for them all along the road but did not find them. Then the king's men went back to the city.

sw.L: Wakaenda, wakafika milimani, wakakaa huko siku tatu, mpaka wale waliowafuatia walipokuwa wamerudi; nao waliowafuatia wakatafuta katika njia yote, wasiwapate.
sw.B: Basi walikwenda vilimani, wakakaa huko siku tatu, mpaka wale waliowafuatia walipokuwa wamerudi. Waliowafuatia walikuwa wametafuta katika njia yote bila kuwapata.
sw.R: Wale wapelelezi walikwenda vilimani, wakajificha huko kwa siku tatu. Watu wa mfalme waliwatafuta katika njia yote, lakini hawakuwapata. Kisha watu hao wa mfalme wakarudi mjini.

es.L: Y ellos fueron y llegaron a la región montañosa y se quedaron allí tres días, hasta que volvieron los perseguidores; y los perseguidores [los] buscaron por todo el camino y no [los] encontraron.
es.B: Así que se fueron a los montes y se quedaron allí tres días, hasta que regresaron los que los perseguían. Los perseguidores los habían buscado por todo el camino sin encontrarlos.
es.R: Los espías se fueron a los montes y se escondieron allí durante tres días. Los hombres del rey los buscaron por todo el camino, pero no los encontraron. Después los hombres del rey volvieron a la ciudad.

decisions.choice: the pursuers searched ... and did not find them
decisions.reason: The search happened while the spies hid, before the pursuers turned back; Rahab's plan (verse 16) worked.

decisions.choice: the search told before the return
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened, and says where the pursuers returned to.

records.literal_gloss: And returned [the] two men and went down from the hill country and crossed over and came to Joshua son of Nun, and recounted to him all the [things] finding them.

en.L: Then the two men returned and came down from the hill country and crossed over, and they came to Joshua son of Nun and told him all that had happened to them.
en.B: Then the two men came back down from the hills, crossed the river and came to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened to them.
en.R: Then the two men came down out of the hills. They crossed the Jordan River and went back to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened.

sw.L: Kisha wale watu wawili wakarudi, wakashuka kutoka milimani, wakavuka, wakafika kwa Yoshua mwana wa Nuni, wakamweleza yote yaliyowapata.
sw.B: Kisha wale watu wawili walishuka kutoka vilimani, wakavuka mto, wakafika kwa Yoshua mwana wa Nuni. Wakamweleza kila kitu kilichowapata.
sw.R: Kisha wale watu wawili walishuka kutoka vilimani. Wakavuka Mto Yordani na kurudi kwa Yoshua mwana wa Nuni. Wakamweleza kila kitu kilichotokea.

es.L: Entonces los dos hombres volvieron y bajaron de la región montañosa y cruzaron, y llegaron a Josué hijo de Nun y le contaron todo lo que les había sucedido.
es.B: Entonces los dos hombres bajaron de los montes, cruzaron el río y llegaron adonde estaba Josué hijo de Nun. Le contaron todo lo que les había sucedido.
es.R: Entonces los dos hombres bajaron de los montes. Cruzaron el río Jordán y volvieron adonde estaba Josué hijo de Nun. Le contaron todo lo que había pasado.

decisions.choice: crossed over: the Jordan
decisions.reason: The river is not named, but they had to cross the Jordan to reach the camp at Shittim (verse 1).

decisions.choice: all that had happened to them: literally "all the things that found them"
decisions.reason: The verb (matsa', "find") is used of events that come upon someone (Genesis 44:34; Numbers 20:14).

decisions.choice: the river (B); the Jordan River (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they crossed (m1).

records.literal_gloss: And they said to Joshua, surely has given YHWH into our hand all the land, and also have melted all [the] inhabitants of the land before us.

en.L: And they said to Joshua, "Truly {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given all the land into our hand; and also all the inhabitants of the land melt away before us."
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has surely handed the whole land over to us," they told Joshua. "Everyone who lives there is melting in fear because of us."
en.R: They said to Joshua, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has really given us the whole land! All the people who live there are weak with fear because of us."

sw.L: Wakamwambia Yoshua, "Hakika {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametia nchi yote mikononi mwetu; na pia wakazi wote wa nchi wanayeyuka mbele yetu."
sw.B: Wakamwambia Yoshua, "Kweli {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameikabidhi nchi yote mikononi mwetu. Wote wanaoishi huko wanayeyuka kwa woga kwa sababu yetu."
sw.R: Wakamwambia Yoshua, "Kweli {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ametupa nchi yote! Watu wote wanaoishi huko wamekosa nguvu kwa sababu ya kutuogopa."

es.L: Y dijeron a Josué: «Verdaderamente {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha entregado toda la tierra en nuestra mano; y además todos los habitantes de la tierra se derriten delante de nosotros».
es.B: Le dijeron a Josué: «De verdad {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos ha entregado toda la tierra. Todos los que viven allí se derriten de miedo ante nosotros».
es.R: Le dijeron a Josué: «¡{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de veras nos ha dado toda la tierra! Toda la gente que vive allí está sin fuerzas por el miedo que nos tiene».

decisions.choice: given into our hand: put in our power
decisions.reason: To give into someone's hand is to give victory over a place or people (6:2; 8:1; 10:8).

decisions.choice: the spies' report echoes Rahab
decisions.reason: Their words take up hers almost exactly (verse 9). Unlike the spies of Numbers 13-14, whose report made the people afraid, these men bring back courage, and it comes from a Canaanite's confession.

decisions.choice: melting in fear (B); weak with fear (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.
